<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},
   "required": ["answer"], "additionalProperties": false}}},
 "logit_bias": {"154843": 100, "154842": 50, "4913": 30, "9214": 30, "788": 30, "330": 30,
                "9689": 30, "9204": 30, "154820": 30}}
```

main, 3 of 3:

```text
HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
(EngineCore pid=131) ERROR 10-14 06:31:44 [scheduler.py:2189] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843] for request chatcmpl-8bf78d42551e682d-8a4ad66a. Terminating request.
```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text
HTTP 200  finish_reason=stop  reasoning="" (no <tool_call>)  content={"answer": "yes"}  tool_calls=[]
```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

Each accepted draft position used a masked row; an unmasked draft row would have sampled `<tool_call>` and failed the request.

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

On main the CPU stand-in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) takes its arguments in an order that no longer matches `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher passes `slot_mapping` as `block_size` and the first forward fails. These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.

I verified this PR on H200 against the production failure we saw on GLM-5.3 (`Failed to advance FSM ... for tokens [..., 154843]`, which surfaces as HTTP 500).

**Why it fixes the bug.** Since #59627, an implicit reasoning end (`<tool_call>`, token 154843 for GLM) is fed to the grammar. The first version of #59627 only did that when `validate_tokens` accepted the token, but that check was removed during review. Reasoning rows are unmasked, so the model can sample `<tool_call>` while thinking. A pure JSON-schema grammar then rejects it, and the scheduler terminates the request. Before #59627 the token was skipped instead, which gave a 200 with empty content. This PR bans such tokens in reasoning rows when the grammar can't start with them. The model ends reasoning with `</think>` instead, so nothing the grammar rejects is ever fed to it. Grammars that do accept `<tool_call>` (required, named, or auto tool tags) are unaffected, so the duplicated `<tool_call>` fix from #59627 is kept.

**Setup.** GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. I compared main (a2fb482732) with this PR (6d144d6478). The failing shape is a conversation whose tool result quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a request with `response_format: json_schema` and a pure JSON grammar, meaning no `tools` or `tool_choice: "none"`.

**Without spec decode**

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tagged tool result, json_schema, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| same, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>` (and blocking `</think>`) | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged tool result, json_schema | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

**With MTP spec decode** (`num_speculative_tokens=3`, Model Runner V2, async scheduling)

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tagged tool result, json_schema, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| same, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged tool result, json_schema | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

The server log on main has one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500. The PR's logs have none and no tracebacks. I also ran the CPU unit path (`StructuredOutputManager` with the GLM tokenizer, xgrammar and guidance): `<tool_call>` is masked in every reasoning row for json_schema and stays allowed for a required tool tag.

Notes:
- The remaining invalid JSON responses are not grammar failures. The raw token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string, and the frontend cuts `content` at that point. That is a separate, pre-existing issue that this PR doesn't touch.
- The `logit_bias` row can't run under spec decode (400). I didn't test the V1 model runner.
- With MTP I needed `--max-num-seqs 256` on both builds, because the default exceeds the Mamba cache blocks. This is unrelated to the PR.

This verification was done with AI assistance (Claude).

@simon-veitner-redhat your H200 run covers what the CPU validation here could not reach: Model Runner V2, async scheduling and MTP. The CPU end to end ran the V1 model runner, so between the two both runners are covered. I moved your results into the description.

Agree the cut content is separate. The parser matches `<tool_call>` as text inside content, so a tag the model quotes in a JSON string ends the content there. `Glm47MoeParser.parse` on `</think>{"answer": "the log shows <tool_call>get_weather<arg_key>city</arg_key> as text"}` returns content `{"answer": "the log shows`, and with no `tools` on the request it also returns a `get_weather` call. Wonder if we could skip the tool-call terminals when the request cannot call tools (no `tools`, or `tool_choice: "none"`). I'll track that separately.

# Reproducing the GLM-5.3 structured-output 500 (PR #61574)

## What fails

GLM-5.3 can end reasoning implicitly by emitting `<tool_call>` (token 154843) instead of `</think>`.
While the request is still reasoning, its grammar bitmask is not applied, so the sampler can pick 154843 freely.
Since #59627, that token is then fed to the request's grammar.
When the grammar is a pure JSON schema (`response_format` with no tools, or `tool_choice: "none"`), it cannot accept `<tool_call>`.
xgrammar rejects the token, the engine logs `Failed to advance FSM`, and the request returns HTTP 500.
Before #59627 the same requests returned a 200 with empty content.

PR #61574 masks implicit reasoning-end tokens in reasoning rows when the grammar cannot start with them.
The model then ends reasoning with `</think>` and produces schema-valid JSON.

With `tools` and `tool_choice: "auto"` the grammar is a structural tag that accepts `<tool_call>`, so that shape does not 500.

## Setup

Two builds of the same tree: main at `a2fb4827` and the PR head `6d144d64`, which is based on that commit.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm && cd vllm
git checkout a2fb4827                                  # "main"
# PR build: git fetch origin pull/61574/head && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .                # Python-only change, precompiled kernels are fine
```

Serve on two GPUs. I used H200s.
The non-spec server below logs `backend='auto'` and selects xgrammar.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --served-model-name glm \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 32768 --port 8000 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47
```

MTP variant with 3 speculative tokens.
Without `--max-num-seqs 256` startup fails for me with `max_num_seqs (1024) exceeds available Mamba cache blocks (1003)`.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --served-model-name glm \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 32768 --port 8000 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## The failing request

The conversation is a `Read` tool call whose result quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`).
The final turn asks for a JSON summary through `response_format: json_schema`.
Seeing the tags in context makes the model emit `<tool_call>` mid-reasoning on most seeds.

`repro_glm_so_500.py` below sends each row with seeds 0..N-1 and prints HTTP codes and JSON validity.
It uses only the standard library.

<details><summary>repro_glm_so_500.py</summary>

```python
# Reproduces the GLM-5.3 "Failed to advance FSM ... for tokens 154843" HTTP 500
# (vllm-project/vllm#61574). Stdlib only. usage: python repro_glm_so_500.py [port] [n]
import json
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "8000"
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8
THINK_END, TOOL_CALL = 154842, 154843  # </think>, <tool_call>

# The tool result quotes GLM's own tool-call tags; that is what makes the model
# emit <tool_call> while still reasoning.
TAGGED = (
    "# Parser notes\n\nGLM-5.3 wraps every function call in <tool_call>...</tool_call>"
    " tags; each argument is <arg_key>k</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value>. Example:"
    " <tool_call>Read<arg_key>file_path</arg_key><arg_value>a.txt</arg_value>"
    "</tool_call>\n"
)
PLAIN = (
    "# Parser notes\n\nGLM-5.3 wraps every function call in tool-call tags; each "
    "argument is a key tag followed by a value tag. Example: a Read call with a "
    "file_path argument.\n"
)
TOOLS = [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read", "description": "Read a file.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path"],
                    "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"}}}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Write", "description": "Write a file.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path", "content"],
                    "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"},
                                   "content": {"type": "string"}}}}},
]
SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}, "mentions_tags": {"type": "boolean"}},
    "required": ["summary", "mentions_tags"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}
RF = {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "summary", "schema": SCHEMA}}


def messages(tool_result):
    return [
        {"role": "user", "content": "Read docs/parser.md, then give me a one-sentence "
         "summary of it and whether it mentions tags."},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1",
         "type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read",
                                          "arguments": "{\"file_path\": \"docs/parser.md\"}"}}]},
        {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": tool_result},
    ]


ROWS = {
    "fail2: tagged + json_schema, no tools field": dict(
        messages=messages(TAGGED), response_format=RF),
    "fail3: tagged + json_schema, tool_choice none": dict(
        messages=messages(TAGGED), tools=TOOLS, response_format=RF, tool_choice="none"),
    "ctl: tagged + json_schema, tool_choice required": dict(
        messages=messages(TAGGED), tools=TOOLS, response_format=RF,
        tool_choice="required"),
    "ctl2: untagged + json_schema, no tools field": dict(
        messages=messages(PLAIN), response_format=RF),
    # Deterministic: forces <tool_call> during reasoning. Spec decode rejects
    # logit_bias with a 400, so this row only applies without MTP.
    "det: logit_bias <tool_call>, json_schema": dict(
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France? Reply "
                   "with a summary and mentions_tags=false."}],
        response_format=RF, temperature=0,
        logit_bias={str(THINK_END): -100, str(TOOL_CALL): 10}),
}


def post(body):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, None


def json_valid(resp):
    try:
        obj = json.loads(resp["choices"][0]["message"].get("content") or "")
        return isinstance(obj, dict) and set(obj) == {"summary", "mentions_tags"}
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        return False


for name, extra in ROWS.items():
    codes, valid = {}, 0
    for seed in range(N):
        code, resp = post({"model": "glm", "max_tokens": 4000, "seed": seed, **extra})
        codes[code] = codes.get(code, 0) + 1
        valid += code == 200 and json_valid(resp)
    print(f"{name:50} codes={codes} 500s={codes.get(500, 0)}/{N} json_valid={valid}/{N}",
          flush=True)
```

</details>

The rows:

| Row | Request shape |

| fail2 | tagged tool result, `response_format`, no `tools` field |

## Expected results

Measured with N=8 on 2xH200, TP2, 2026-10-14. Cells are HTTP 500 counts out of 8, with valid JSON counts in parentheses.

| Row | main | PR | main + MTP | PR + MTP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fail2 | **7/8** (0) | 0/8 (4) | **6/8** (2) | 0/8 (6) |
| fail3 | **5/8** (3) | 0/8 (7) | **2/8** (6) | 0/8 (8) |
| ctl | 0/8 (0) | 0/8 (0) | 0/8 (0) | 0/8 (0) |
| ctl2 | 0/8 (8) | 0/8 (8) | 0/8 (8) | 0/8 (8) |
| det | **8/8** (0) | 0/8 (0) | 400 | 400 |

The `det` row returns 400 under MTP because spec decode rejects `logit_bias`.
Without MTP, the PR returns 200 with `finish_reason: "stop"` and empty content (the bias blocks `</think>`). That row only checks that the 500 is gone.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},

```

main, 3 of 3:

```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text

```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.

**Why it fixes the bug.** Since #59627, an implicit reasoning end (`<tool_call>`, token 154843 for GLM) is fed to the grammar. The model ends reasoning with `</think>` instead, so nothing the grammar rejects is ever fed to it. Grammars that do accept `<tool_call>` (required, named, or auto tool tags) are unaffected, so the duplicated `<tool_call>` fix from #59627 is kept.

# Reproducing the GLM-5.3 structured-output 500 (PR #61574)

## What fails

GLM-5.3 can end reasoning implicitly by emitting `<tool_call>` (token 154843) instead of `</think>`.
While the request is still reasoning, its grammar bitmask is not applied, so the sampler can pick 154843 freely.
Since #59627, that token is then fed to the request's grammar.
When the grammar is a pure JSON schema (`response_format` with no tools, or `tool_choice: "none"`), it cannot accept `<tool_call>`.
xgrammar rejects the token, the engine logs `Failed to advance FSM`, and the request returns HTTP 500.
Before #59627 the same requests returned a 200 with empty content.

PR #61574 masks implicit reasoning-end tokens in reasoning rows when the grammar cannot start with them.
The model then ends reasoning with `</think>` and produces schema-valid JSON.

With `tools` and `tool_choice: "auto"` the grammar is a structural tag that accepts `<tool_call>`, so that shape does not 500.

## Setup

Two builds of the same tree: main at `a2fb4827` and the PR head `6d144d64`, which is based on that commit.

  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 32768 --port 8000 \
